decisions: One get playback per attempt from the current position to end_utc (end of the local day), scale 1/1, event_type [1,2], client_id 1, channels [0] (the verified request). If the camera ends early (stream_status finished, relay closes the tunnel) and the clip list has a later recording, a new request starts there; otherwise STOPPED with reason 'end of recordings' (constant END_OF_RECORDINGS; StreamState enum unchanged).

Pacing in Python: each TS part is split at video PES starts, their 90 kHz PTS (X-Data-PTS fallback for non-TS-aligned parts) schedule the writes into ffmpeg; the blocked pump stops reading/acking, so the camera's ack window bounds buffering. More than 1 s behind schedule restarts the clock instead of racing.
Position = PTS mapped to UTC: steps <= 3 s advance; bigger jumps (new file) or running past a clip's end snap to the next clip of the list. on_position about 5x per second.

pause(): pump holds the next frame, stall watchdog suspended, best-effort 'do pause'; resume(): 'do play "null"'. A connection the camera dropped while paused reconnects from the last position on resume.

seek(): fresh playback request at the time (verified path, no stale data mixing); the spec's in-session 'do play {start_time}' is implemented only in the mocks. Seek also resumes a paused playback and restarts after the end.
set_speed(): 1/1, 2/1, 4/1, 8/1 applied by the client pacing; the request always says scale 1/1 (only verified value). The effective speed is bounded by how fast the camera/relay delivers.

Limiter: playback uses the same limiter key as live view (host / deviceId), so live + playback = the camera's 2 media sessions. Relay playback takes no RemoteStreamGate slot. FAILED 'limit' reasons become PLAYBACK_LIMIT_MESSAGE (asks to close live view / other apps).
Controller: separate per-camera 'playback' strand; the service is created but not connected (no control login needed for playback). Default frame size 1280x720, letterboxed by the window.

PlayerWindow: top-level non-modal QWidget, one per camera (registry in PlaybackPanel.player_window()); seek on timeline click or drag release; date change stops, reloads clips and starts at the first clip.

open_issues: Not verified on real cameras: continuing across a clip boundary within one request, the end-of-day / end-of-recordings path, and speeds > 1x (all covered by mocks only).
Seek latency is a full reconnect: about 1-2 s on the LAN, about 3 s over the relay (new slot). The spec's in-session do play {start_time} could be faster but is unverified.
The timeline always shows the whole local day (no zoom); one-minute clips are a few pixels wide.
Live view and playback of one camera share its 2 media sessions; a third viewer (e.g. the phone app) makes playback fail with PLAYBACK_LIMIT_MESSAGE.
